solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: I hand Pimms out, one in schooner perhaps

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of the drinker's words are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone serving Pimm's on a sailing boat hands one to a crew member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges I HAND PIMMS; 'perhaps' tells you a schooner is only one example of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A junior naval officer serves aboard a ship, and a schooner is one kind of sailing vessel.

clue.text: People taking in island air

indicators.note: taking in means the word for people holds the island letter within it

parts.note: people are men, in the general old sense

explanation.surface: A crowd breathing in the atmosphere of an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Air in the sense of a person's manner or bearing is a synonym.

clue.text: Uncompromising doctor with cold drinks wine

indicators.note: drinks means the doctor-and-cold pair swallows the wine, holding it inside

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: A hard-line doctor knocks back wine with a cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe, extreme measures are uncompromising ones; the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Can holy ritual somehow be producing visions?

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of the ritual phrase are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: A question whether a religious ceremony could make worshippers see things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges CAN HOLY RITUAL; 'be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that brings on hallucinations, seeing things not there, produces visions.

clue.text: Stick in front of plane certainly for take-off

indicators.note: front of picks the opening letter of the word plane
in places the stick inside the word for certainly

parts.note: ay (aye) is an old word of assent, meaning yes certainly
a rod is a stick

explanation.surface: Advice to put a stick at the front of an aircraft so it can take off safely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take-off' looks like an aircraft leaving the ground, but it is an imitation that mocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A take-off is a mocking imitation, which is what a spoof or burlesque is.

clue.text: Officers laid arms all over the place

indicators.note: all over the place says the letters of the two words are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Military officers putting down their weapons untidily everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' rearranges LAID ARMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Admirals are the most senior naval officers.

clue.text: Hunk's small short dog

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes
lab is the short form of labrador, a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A muscular man's little dog is a stunted one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hunk' suggests a handsome man, but here it means a thick piece of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunk of stone or cake is a thick, solid piece, as a slab is.

clue.text: French tongue — clipped or showing listlessness?

indicators.note: clipped means the French word has its final letter trimmed off

parts.note: langue is French for language or tongue
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question whether a languid manner shows in a curt French accent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clipped' removes the final E of LANGUE; 'showing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Languor is a dreamy lack of energy, a synonym for listlessness.

clue.text: Bald, racked characters reincarnated in TV comedy

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are given new life in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A bald, tortured figure is brought back to life in a TV sitcom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters reincarnated' rearranges BALD RACKED. Blackadder is a long-running British BBC sitcom set in different historical eras, its hero reborn in each series.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackadder is a classic British television sitcom starring Rowan Atkinson, so it is an example.

clue.text: English novelist — he sends a message

parts.note: Norman Mailer was an American novelist

explanation.surface: Describing an English writer of novels who is also a correspondent.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sends an electronic letter is one who mails, so the description fits.

clue.text: Deep Purple get a man rocking

indicators.note: rocking says the letters of the three words are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: The rock band Deep Purple gets a man rocking out to their music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deep Purple' looks like the rock band, but it is a colour; 'rocking' rearranges GET A MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Magenta is a deep purplish-red colour, so a deep purple describes it.

clue.text: I don't believe you, on top of all the rage, escape punishment

indicators.note: in a down clue, on top of puts the first phrase above the second

parts.note: get away! is an exclamation of disbelief
with it means fashionable, all the rage

explanation.surface: Someone's disbelief on top of their anger about escaping punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: To get off scot-free for wrongdoing is the idiom's meaning: escaping punishment.

clue.text: Business is booming at first having experienced shock

indicators.note: at first puts the booming piece before the business piece

parts.note: something booming thunders
truck means dealings or business, as in having no truck with

explanation.surface: A business doing very well at first, then suddenly suffering a shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Business is booming' reads as one stock phrase, but it splits in two, and 'at first' tells you the second half leads the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stunned or astounded is a synonym for having been shocked.

clue.text: Composing bogus poems is a sign one's scared

indicators.note: composing means putting the letters of the two words together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Writing fake poems as a symptom of fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Small bumps rising on the skin are a bodily reaction to fear or cold.

clue.text: Sea monster covered up bloomer

parts.note: an orc is a sea monster in old legend, as well as a killer whale
hid means concealed, covered up

explanation.surface: A sea monster concealed a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a blunder, but here it is something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer here means a plant that flowers, and this exotic plant is one.

clue.text: Blossomed following getting depressed

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
lowered means pushed down, depressed

explanation.surface: A plant bloomed after becoming low.
explanation.definitionFit: Blossomed and bloomed are synonyms for producing flowers.

clue.text: Verbally abused an unpleasant woman

indicators.note: verbally points to how the phrase is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: harried means harassed or abused, followed by an as written

explanation.surface: A nasty woman was shouted at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Verbally' looks part of the abuse, but it signals that HARRIED AN, said aloud, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A harridan is a bossy, belligerent old woman, an unpleasant one.

clue.text: Illegal passenger's expressions of pain and disgust going into hold

indicators.note: going into places the two exclamations inside the word for hold

parts.note: stay means hold or restrain
ow is a cry of pain
aw is an exclamation of disgust or dismay

explanation.surface: A stowed-away traveller groaning while hidden in a ship's hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold' suggests a ship's cargo space, but it is a verb meaning stay; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who hides aboard a ship or plane to travel without paying is an illegal passenger.

clue.text: Soldiers secure old holiday resort

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
to land something is to secure it

explanation.surface: Troops taking possession of an old vacation spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Orlando in Florida is a famous holiday destination for its theme parks.

clue.text: Some Caerphilly cheese as dessert item

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some Welsh cheese served as a pudding course.
explanation.walkthrough: Changed from the draft: 'as' is a link, not part of the definition, since 'as dessert item' cannot stand in for a fruit. Caerphilly is a crumbly Welsh cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: This small sweet Chinese fruit is often served as a dessert.

clue.text: Wizard boarding school's not right having hard bunk

indicators.note: not takes the right abbreviation out of the school name

parts.note: Hogwarts is the wizarding boarding school in the Harry Potter books
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A wizard school lacking moral standards with tough sleeping quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bunk' looks like a bed in a boarding school, but it means nonsense; 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunk, short for bunkum, means nonsense, as does this slang word.

clue.text: A spirit favouring youth

parts.note: Geist is German for spirit, used in English in zeitgeist and poltergeist

explanation.surface: A ghost that prefers the young.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone prejudiced against older people favours the young, so the description fits.

clue.text: Labour politician mostly turned to tackle electoral fraud

indicators.note: mostly means the politician's surname loses its final letter

parts.note: Ed Balls is a former Labour cabinet minister in Britain

indicators.note: turned means the little word to is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
rigging is a ship's tackle, its ropes and gear

explanation.surface: A Labour politician mostly trying to deal with vote-cheating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts BALLS to BALL; 'turned' makes OT of TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Fixing the counting of votes is a kind of electoral fraud.

clue.text: A former railway charity

parts.note: LMS was the London, Midland and Scottish Railway, a pre-nationalisation British line

explanation.surface: An old railway company turned into a charitable body.
explanation.definitionFit: Alms are gifts of money or food to the poor, a form of charity.

clue.text: Rich person takes year in popular holiday area

indicators.note: in puts the person and year inside the holiday area

parts.note: the Med, the Mediterranean, is a popular holiday region
one means a person, as in one should

explanation.surface: A wealthy person spends a year abroad at a favourite resort region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rich person' reads as one unit, but 'Rich' alone is the definition; 'takes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a lot of money means being wealthy, which rich describes.

clue.text: Abraham's son is married, embraced by Jacob's wife contrarily

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: embraced by puts the married letter inside the backward name
contrarily means the wife's name runs in the opposite direction

parts.note: Leah was the first wife of Jacob in Genesis

explanation.surface: A biblical son is married into the family of Jacob's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrarily' turns LEAH into HAEL, which takes M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Ishmael was Abraham's first son, born to Hagar.

clue.text: In Kent area, see fruit

indicators.note: In places the word for see inside the region abbreviation

parts.note: SE, the south-east of England, is the region containing the county of Kent
lo is an old word for see or behold

explanation.surface: An invitation to look at fruit growing in Kent, the Garden of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the small sour fruit of the blackthorn, used to flavour gin.

clue.text: Laughing uncontrollably this month is irritating

parts.note: inst., short for instant, means this month in old business letters
itches means is irritating

explanation.surface: This month has been bothersome.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in fits of laughter is the idiom's meaning, laughing helplessly.
